<a id="s0-p1"></a>[0¶1] This document is the contract for the data tables `pcrec` prints about its own registries: `--list-syntax`, `--list-verbs`, `--list-families`, `--list-axes` and `--list-definitions`. For each it states every column by header name with its value set, and which values are a closed vocabulary a consumer may switch on versus free text a consumer may only display. The wire format every table shares (`#` comments, one header row, append-only columns, resolve-by-name) is `docs/spec/table_contract.md`; what each flag answers, in prose, is `docs/spec/cli.md` §2. Every value set below can be re-read from a build with the command given beside it. The listings' history is `docs/dev/history/registry_record.md`, which is not normative.

<a id="s1"></a>
## 1. The shape of the promise

<a id="s1-p1"></a>[1¶1] Columns are added at the END of a table; a consumer resolves a column by its HEADER NAME, never by hardcoded position or field count; a column is never removed, renamed or reordered (`table_contract.md` §2¶4, §3¶1). The rule holds before and after v1; after v1 it is a compatibility promise (`match_api.md` §0¶4). A consumer that hardcoded a field count breaks on an appended column; one that resolves by name does not.

<a id="s1-p2"></a>[1¶2] `tests/lib/table.sh` is the shell and awk implementation of resolve-by-name. `tests/registry/compliance_section.py` carries its own column list and cross-checks it against the dump's live header on every run (§7¶4), so the two implementations cannot disagree about a header.

<a id="s1-p3"></a>[1¶3] The registry's generating structure (`RegRow`, `src/core/internal.h`) is the single declarative source: one row per spelling, read by the parser, the reject-test suite, `--explain` and the generated index in `docs/pcre2_compliance.md`. This document describes what the dumps built from that source print, not the row struct.

<a id="s2"></a>
## 2. `--list-syntax` — one line per construct spelling

<a id="s2-p1"></a>[2¶1] The header is the last `#` line before the first data row; the table has 17 columns:

    #kind  selector  syntax  module  feature  flavours  engines  status
    diag  flags  expect  note  roadmap  quantifiable  class_expect
    built  family

<a id="s2-p2"></a>[2¶2] A consumer must not hardcode the row count. `tests/registry/registry_check.c` pins the exact count and the `checked`/`built`/`unbuilt`/`na` totals, and fails when a row is added or removed without its pin moving.

| column | value set | stable? |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `esc` \| `group` \| `verb` \| `class-bracket` \| `quant-suffix` \| `bare` — the six `RegKind` doorways. `quant-suffix` and `bare` have no lexical doorway: a possessive suffix is recognised inside `p_rep` after the quantifier is parsed, and `^`, `$`, the plain capturing group `(...)` and `${name}` are parsed directly in `p_atom`/`p_group_body`. The dumps and the definitions machinery read these rows; nothing on the live parse path does | yes |
| `selector` | the byte after the doorway that selects the row: a printable ASCII character, `\xHH` for any other byte, or `*` for the catch-all row of a kind (`REG_SEL_ANY`). A `quant-suffix` row's selector is its quantifier byte, so `*` there is the literal `*` | yes; not a short closed list, read per row |
| `syntax` | a pattern that PROBES the construct; `tests/reject/` and `--explain` compile it. Every row's value is itself a valid probe pattern (`registry_check`'s well-formedness pass) | free text |
| `module` | the owning module name, empty for `status` `base`/`rejected` rows with no owning module. The names are the `--features` roster (`cli.md` §1): `assertions`, `atomic-groups`, `backrefs`, `branch-reset`, `callouts`, `classes`, `comments`, `conditionals`, `extended-classes`, `lookaround`, `misc`, `modifiers`, `named-groups`, `quoting`, `recursion`, `ucp`, `unicode-props`, `vars`, `verbs` (`cut -f4 \| sort -u`) | yes |
| `feature` | a hex bitmask. Not independently named here: `registry.c`'s `M_<module>` macros already pair each bit with a module name, and a second bit-to-name table would be a second home. Read `module` beside it; `tests/registry/` proves the two are a bijection | yes |
| `flavours` | `pcre2`, the only value; `--flavour` (`cli.md` §2) filters on it | yes |
| `engines` | empty \| `vm` \| `dfa\|vm` — which engine(s) can execute a produced node for the row; empty for rows with no producer or no engine question (`status` not `module`) | yes |
| `status` | `base` \| `module` \| `rejected` (`RegStatus`): base-tier grammar, grammar gated behind a module, or a construct pcrec refuses outright | yes |
| `diag` | `none` \| `module` \| `module-octal` \| `fixed` — which diagnostic TEMPLATE the row's refusal uses (`RegDiag`); pairs with `expect` | yes |
| `flags` | empty \| `class-delim` \| `lexical` — a mask rendering of `RegFlags`; a row carrying both would print both | yes |
| `expect` | the SUBSTRING the diagnostic must contain when the row's syntax is refused (a substring of the doorway's template, so the template has one home); empty for rows that compile cleanly at base tier | free text |
| `note` | one-line human description | free text |
| `roadmap` | `-` (the question does not arise, base rows) \| `planned` \| `never`. `registry_check` enforces the legal pairing with `status`/`diag`; a `never` row must not promise a module in its diagnostic | yes |
| `quantifiable` | `yes` \| `no` \| `form` \| `lexical` \| `-` — whether `<syntax>*` is grammatically legal after the construct, measured against libpcre2 and re-verified by `tests/spec_mod0/check10` | yes |
| `class_expect` | the measured class-POSITION behaviour: `char N`, `set N` or `err N`, or EMPTY — not `-` — for a construct that cannot reach a class position (the header's "empty field = none" rule) | yes as a vocabulary shape; values are per-construct facts |
| `built` | `built` \| `unbuilt` \| `defect` \| `-`; §3 | yes |
| `family` | the canonical `syntax` of the family the row is a spelling of; empty when the row is its own family; §5 | free text; when set it is always another row's `syntax` |

<a id="s2-p3"></a>[2¶3] The `built`/`unbuilt`/`-` split is witnessed by `build/pcrec --list-syntax | grep -v '^#' | cut -f16 | sort | uniq -c`.

<a id="s3"></a>
## 3. `built` versus `status`/`roadmap` — two different questions

<a id="s3-p1"></a>[3¶1] `status` and `roadmap` are PCRE2 and base-grammar facts, fixed when the row is authored: is this real syntax, and does pcrec plan to implement it. `built` is orthogonal: has THIS construct's producer landed in this build. It is derived live by driving the row's own `syntax` through a gate-forced-open doorway call (`pcrec_construct_built_status`, `src/dump/syntax_dump.c`), never a hand-declared field, because a hand-kept column would have to be synchronised with the ports by hand — the two-homes shape the registry exists to prevent. A row can be `status` `module`, `roadmap` `planned` and `built` `unbuilt` at once; that is the ordinary case for a module partway through its rollout.

<a id="s3-p2"></a>[3¶2] The values: `built` — the row's producer stamped a node. `unbuilt` — the gate-forced-open probe still refused; with every module open, only a missing producer can refuse a well-formed row. `-` — the question does not arise (`status` is `base` or `rejected`). `defect` — never printed by a well-formed registry: it is the outcome `registry_check.c` asserts against, for a row whose own `syntax` yields neither a clean answer nor the unbuilt refusal shape. A lexical row (`flags` `lexical`) is `built` through a dedicated arm of `pcrec_construct_built_status`, because its producer is a lexer-mode transition with no doorway return to classify.

<a id="s4"></a>
## 4. `--list-verbs` — the `(*VERB)` name tables

<a id="s4-p1"></a>[4¶1] PCRE2 keeps two case-selected verb-name tables; the dump prints both. It has 6 columns:

    #table  name  forms  unknown  roadmap  quantifiable

| column | value set | stable? |
|---|---|---|
| `table` | `upper` \| `lower` — which table, selected by the case of the name's first byte | yes |
| `name` | the verb's bare name | free text (a fixed vocabulary, not enumerated here) |
| `forms` | a `\|`-joined subset of `(*N)`, `(*N:a)`, `(*N:)`, `(*N=d)`, `arg-is-subpattern`, `start-of-pattern-only` | the token vocabulary is fixed; which subset applies is per name |
| `unknown` | the fixed diagnostic text for an unrecognised name in this table | free text, identical for every row of a table |
| `roadmap` | `planned` \| `never` (never `-`: every verb name has a disposition) | yes |
| `quantifiable` | `yes` \| `no` \| `not-askable` — `not-askable` is distinct from `no`: the unquantified form itself does not compile (for example a start-of-pattern-only verb away from position 0), so "is `X*` legal" cannot be posed | yes |

<a id="s4-p2"></a>[4¶2] `forms` is what libpcre2 ACCEPTS, measured, not what pcrec implements; a consumer reading `forms` as "what pcrec will parse" is reading the wrong column.

<a id="s5"></a>
## 5. `--list-families` — the grouping index

<a id="s5-p1"></a>[5¶1] A family is the set of `--list-syntax` rows sharing a key, where a row's key is its `family` cell if set and its own `syntax` otherwise. The dump prints one line per family. It has 7 columns:

    #syntax  module  engines  status  built  nmembers  members

| column | value set | stable? |
|---|---|---|
| `syntax` | the family's KEY: always some row's own `syntax`, the canonical spelling | free text, traceable to a `--list-syntax` row |
| `module` | taken from the family's first member in table order | yes |
| `engines` | taken from the first member | yes |
| `status` | taken from the first member | yes |
| `built` | `built` if EVERY member is `built`; `-` if no member's `built` is anything but `-`; otherwise `unbuilt` | yes |
| `nmembers` | the number of spellings in the family, at least 1; a family of one prints what `--list-syntax` prints for that row | count |
| `members` | every spelling, space-separated, in table order, the canonical member first when it is itself a row | free text |

<a id="s5-p2"></a>[5¶2] `module`, `engines` and `status` are read off the first member rather than elected independently, because `registry_check.c` asserts that every member of a family agrees on all three; a disagreement fails there, not silently here.

<a id="s5-p3"></a>[5¶3] The direction of `built` matters: a family whose canonical spelling compiles while one alias does not is not a built family. Grouping is an index-layer fact and never changes a row's dispatch identity: `--list-syntax` still gives every alias its own line and its own probe, because `tests/reject/` tests each independently.

<a id="s5-p4"></a>[5¶4] `--list-families` takes no `--flavour` (`cli.md` §2): a family is a grouping OF rows, and filtering members mid-grouping would make `built` answer a different question per invocation.

<a id="s6"></a>
## 6. `--list-axes` — the optimization-axis registry

<a id="s6-p1"></a>[6¶1] The dump describes the compiler's own tuning machinery rather than PCRE2 syntax: for every axis where the compiler chooses among two or more emitted strategies for a pattern, one row per (axis, candidate), in the emitter's PREFERENCE order (order 1 is tried first; the last candidate of an axis always applies). The leading table has 12 columns:

    #axis  order  candidate  kind  stamp_macro  stamp_value  deny_macro
    deny_bit  force_macro  force_bit  cli_flag  applies

<a id="s6-p2"></a>[6¶2] The table is the leading anonymous table of a stream that continues with the named section `memfn` (§6¶6). Its rows are selected with `build/pcrec --list-axes | bash tests/lib/table.sh table-main -`. Row and axis counts move with every axis that lands; a consumer reads them live and never from this document. The distinct values of the `axis` column are the axis roster; `docs/spec/tuning.md` §2 documents each axis, and `tests/registry/axes_registry_check.sh` requires every documented `(bit N)` heading to have a dumped row at that bit and every dumped bit to have a heading.

| column | value set | stable? |
|---|---|---|
| `axis` | the axis name | yes; append-only — a new axis is a new value |
| `order` | a positive integer, 1-based, dense per axis (N candidates use 1..N) | yes |
| `candidate` | free text; where a stamp exists it is that axis's own stamp vocabulary | yes as a vocabulary shape; values are per axis |
| `kind` | `list` — a real candidate list or table exists in the emitter and the row's `candidate`/`deny_macro` come straight off it. This includes the fallback axes `engine-route`, `size-term` and `prefilter-lang` (cells of the fallback tables, listed in the order the tables walk them), the whole-table axes `fallback` and `prefilter-admit` (one row per table row; they carry no stamp macro) and the seven START axes `prefilter`, `search-start`, `req-admit`, `req-use`, `hyb-reseed`, `vm-anchor-bound` and `end-window` (rows of the one start table `cand_rows[]`). \| `both` — axis `direction` only: not a preference list, both candidates are ALWAYS emitted, once each, per machine. \| `predicate` — no candidate list exists as data; the row is hand-stated from `lib/pcrec.h`'s enum symbols and `tuning.md`'s prose | yes |
| `stamp_macro` | the `#define` the candidate is reported through (for example `RX_DFA_TABLE`, `RX_VM_STRATS`), or empty when no such macro exists (emitter-internal decisions with no observable trace). It may be a macro of another axis's family: the `first-class` row of `prefilter` names `RX_VM_START_SCAN`. A few `predicate` axes stamp an ACTIVITY COUNT rather than a named value (`RX_ALTCLS_MERGES`, `RX_VM_CALL_SPLICED`/`_LINKED`, `RX_FAST_FRAMES`) | yes as a vocabulary shape |
| `stamp_value` | the value `stamp_macro` takes when the candidate is chosen; empty when `stamp_macro` is empty or a count. Where a macro's value set is wider than a two-candidate pair — because the artifact reports WHY a selection landed, or composes a fact from more than one machine — the axis carries ONE ROW PER VALUE, and a row with no lever of its own (empty `deny_macro`/`force_macro`/`cli_flag`) still carries its real `stamp_value` | free text; always another column's own value when non-empty |
| `deny_macro` / `deny_bit` | the `PCREC_NO_*` bit (`lib/pcrec.h`) that removes the candidate from the selection walk, empty when none exists. A candidate removed by EITHER of several bits carries them all, `\|`-joined lowest bit first, in lockstep with `cli_flag` (the `run-pinned` rows: `PCREC_NO_OFFSET_SKIP\|PCREC_NO_RUN_PREFILTER`, `16\|32`, `-fno-offset-skip\|-fno-run-prefilter`); a reader splits all three cells on `\|` together. On a start axis the deny bit may name a FACT's bit rather than the row's own: on the anchored rows of `vm-anchor-bound` `-fno-vm-anchor-bound`, and on `end-window`'s `window` row `-fno-end-window`, empty the landmark the row reads, removing the row's population without removing the row. Axis `prefilter` has no deny flag for the DFA scan's own candidate-start filter | yes |
| `force_macro` / `force_bit` | the `PCREC_FORCE_*` bit that forces the candidate over auto-selection; empty on every row that has none (`vm-prefilter`, `prefilter-lang`, `startpos-guard`, `utf-check`, `comments` and `memfn-simd` carry one) | yes |
| `cli_flag` | the `-f`/`-fno-`/`--engine=` spelling that reaches `deny_macro`/`force_macro`; empty for a candidate reached only as a fallback (no flag REQUESTS a fallback; it is what remains when nothing else applies) | free text; an existing CLI spelling (`cli.md` §1) |
| `applies` | a one-line English summary of the candidate's selection condition | free text, hand-authored (§6¶4) |

<a id="s6-p3"></a>[6¶3] The `table` and `size-term` axes show the one-row-per-value rule. `table` has four rows: `premultiplied` and `indexed` (the per-machine choices, read live) and the artifact-level composites `none` and `mixed` (`kind` `predicate`, hand-stated, orders 3 and 4). `size-term` has seven, in the order `src/core/compile.c` tests them: `option`, `denied`, `default`, `cap-rescue`, `size-model`, `capacity-declined`, `size-model-declined`; only `denied` carries a lever (`PCREC_NO_SIZE_TERM`, `-fno-size-term`).

<a id="s6-p4"></a>[6¶4] **Source boundary.** For the `list` and `both` axes, `candidate`, `deny_macro` and `deny_bit` are read live off the same arrays the emitter's selection walks read (`src/dump/axes_dump.c`'s accessor calls): `dfa_select`'s lists for the machine-form axes, and for the start axes the rows of `cand_rows[]` that `cand_select` walks, each listed under its axis by the row's own `list[route]` column. A candidate landing in one of those arrays appears with no edit to the dump. `applies` is hand-authored prose throughout: `emitter_form.md`'s "applies when" column for the machine-form rows, the row's `desc` for a start axis, the row's `axlist` cell for the three fallback axes, generated from the row's own cells for `fallback` and `prefilter-admit`, and `tuning.md` §2's prose for the `predicate` rows. It is a description, never a live evaluation, because evaluating a predicate needs a pattern a context-free listing does not have. The dump therefore proves what the compiler THINKS its axes are; it is not independent evidence that a stamp or a flag behaves as described. `tests/codegen/run_dfa_stamps.sh` (which reads emitted artifacts) and `tuning.md` §2's differentials (compile twice, compare answers) are the independent side of that claim, and `tests/registry/axes_registry_check.sh` is the independent side of the dump itself (§7¶5).

<a id="s6-p5"></a>[6¶5] `--list-axes` takes no `--flavour`: it reports what THIS BUILD thinks its machinery is, never a claim about PCRE2 syntax. It takes no pattern and no `-o`; it is a syntax query (`cli.md` §1).

<a id="s6-p6"></a>[6¶6] **The `memfn` section.** After the axis table the stream carries `#section memfn`: the option registry of pcrec-memory-functions, the in-tree search-code kit (`docs/design/memfn/integration.md` §R4.4.1). One row per entry of the kit's `mf_options()`, read from the kit; pcrec's dump names no row. The section has 6 columns:

    #name  kind  budget  layer  spelling  doc

| column | value set |
|---|---|
| `name` | the kit's option id, `[a-z0-9-]`, architecture-blind |
| `kind` | `deny` (reached only as `--memfn=no-NAME`) \| `pair` (also forced as `--memfn=NAME`) |
| `budget` | `scan` \| `loop` \| `any` |
| `layer` | `scalar` \| `simd` — the acceptance reading that owns the row; a `simd` row is inert at `-fno-memfn-simd` |
| `spelling` | the accepted `--memfn=` spelling(s), `\|`-joined |
| `doc` | one line, the kit's |

<a id="s6-p7"></a>[6¶7] A row is reached by `--memfn=no-NAME` (bare `NAME` for a `pair` row), a config's raw `pcrec --memfn=` line, or `pcrec_options.memfn` (`cli.md` §1): one opaque string pcrec validates only through the kit and copies into every site. A `simd` row given at `-fno-memfn-simd` is accepted and inert. These rows are not pcrec axes: none carries a `lib/pcrec.h` bit, `src/core/axes.def` has no row for one, and the answer-identity sweep, the identity gates and the registry check read them from this section, never from a list of their own. Each is a kit change's own deny, born with the change that moves an emitted byte.

<a id="s6-p8"></a>[6¶8] The section's independent control is a member-count FLOOR pinned in this document as a literal, sharing no source with the kit's registry. It takes the form of the backquoted name `memfn`, then the words "section floor", a colon and a number, written once in this document and raised in every change that adds a kit row. The kit defines no option at present, so the section is a header only and no floor is pinned; `tests/registry/axes_registry_check.sh` then reports the floor arm as UNREACHED (never as a pass) and FAILS if a row appears with no floor pinned.

<a id="s6-p9"></a>[6¶9] **Reachability of the multi-row values.** On a stock build, `default` (`a(b|c)+d`), `option` (`a(b|c)+d --unroll=4`), `denied` (`a(b|c)+d -fno-size-term`) and `size-model` (the nested-repeat pattern `tests/codegen/run_size_term.sh` calls `NEST8`, with `--features all`) are reached directly, and `table`'s `none` (`\B\b` with `--features all`, a proven-empty engine, `RX_DFA_SCAN "empty"`) and `mixed` (`[01]*1[01]{13}`) likewise. `cap-rescue` and `capacity-declined` are reached by no pattern-and-flags combination on a stock build; `tests/codegen/run_size_term.sh` reaches them through a reference compiler built with a lowered `PCREC_SIZE_TERM_THRESHOLD`/`PCREC_MAX_VM_EMIT_CODE_BYTES`, because the CLI can only raise those limits. `size-model-declined` has no cited natural witness.

<a id="s7"></a>
## 7. What the tests pin, and what they do not

1. <a id="s7-p1"></a>[7¶1] `registry_check.c` (`tests/registry/`) is pcrec checking pcrec: table-versus-parser self-consistency in both directions, the exact `--list-syntax` row count, the `roadmap`/`quantifiable`/`class_expect` legal-pairing rules, kind coverage, and the derived-column assertions (the `defect` outcome, the family rule of §5). It catches a row naming the wrong module or a malformed pairing; it cannot catch a row plausibly wrong on both sides at once, because the wrongness is what both sides read.
2. <a id="s7-p2"></a>[7¶2] PC-3 (`pcre2_check.c`, same directory) closes that gap: it asks libpcre2, independently, whether an `RS_MODULE` row's construct exists in PCRE2 and whether an `RS_REJECTED` row's diagnostic matches PCRE2's own rejection, plus generated differentials (byte sweeps, the class-bracket doorway, POSIX names). PC-4 (`pc4_check.c`) is the semantic differential: what a produced construct MATCHES, cell by cell. PC-3 guarantees that every `RS_MODULE`/`RS_REJECTED` row's existence claim against PCRE2 is independently checked. It says nothing about `built` (a pcrec-only fact) and nothing about `class_expect`'s measured value beyond what its generated cells cover.
3. <a id="s7-p3"></a>[7¶3] PC-3 carries a VERSION FLOOR, libpcre2 10.46 (`PCREC_PCRE2_FLOOR_{MAJOR,MINOR}` in `pcre2_check.c`). A resolved libpcre2 older than the floor, or none, SKIPS with a banner naming the floor and the resolved version, rather than running checks written against constructs only the floor and newer have. The POSIX-class-names probe count is a FLOOR per resolved version, not a pin (`expect_probes_floor()`): it reads the resolved library binary's own ASCII strings, a property of the (version, toolchain, build) triple, so the check asserts `>=` the smallest known-good measurement and prints a `RECORD:` line naming each measured value per box. Every other `expect_probes()` count iterates pcrec-owned tables and is an exact pin.
4. <a id="s7-p4"></a>[7¶4] `compliance_section.py` (the generator of `docs/pcre2_compliance.md`'s "Registry construct index") renders the same 17-column dump. Its `COLS` list is cross-checked against the dump's header line on every run, which is `table_contract.md` §5¶2 (GENERATOR AGREEMENT) applied to this consumer.
5. <a id="s7-p5"></a>[7¶5] `axes_registry_check.sh` (`tests/registry/`) is §6's independent side. It reads `--list-axes` against `docs/spec/tuning.md` §2 (every documented `(bit N)` heading has a dumped row at that bit, and conversely); against the SHIPPED PARSER (every dumped `cli_flag` is a spelling `build/pcrec` accepts — it RUNS the flag; it does not read `cli/main.c`'s text, because the parser's spellings and the dump's `cli_flag` column are one row of `src/core/axes.def`, and comparing the two would compare a table with itself); and against `docs/spec/match_api.md` §6.3 (every dumped `stamp_value` is a value that macro's value-set table lists there, and conversely; the D46 bit constants' value set is read from the literal `#define` block in `src/gen/emit_dfa.c`, because they are emitted-artifact text `lib/pcrec.h` never declares). Every discrepancy is named by name, not by count alone. It also holds the `memfn` floor arm of §6.
6. <a id="s7-p6"></a>[7¶6] `definitions_check.c` and `run_definitions_tests.sh` (`tests/registry/`) are the checks of §9; `run_definitions_oracle.sh` is the option-matrix self-oracle of §9¶6.

<a id="s8"></a>
## 8. Retired

<a id="s8-p1"></a>[8¶1] Retired. The section held a landing note for the first revision of this document; it stated no contract. Its text is in `docs/dev/history/registry_record.md`.

<a id="s9"></a>
## 9. `--list-definitions` — the replacement/definition table

<a id="s9-p1"></a>[9¶1] The dump prints, per registry row, the core-syntax definition(s) that row's construct reduces to under each option scope. It has 7 columns:

    #kind  selector  syntax  order  predicate  definition  applies

| column | value set | stable? |
|---|---|---|
| `kind`/`selector`/`syntax` | the same three columns §2 prints for the owning row, rendered by the same helpers (`kind_name`/`put_selector` in `src/dump/syntax_dump.c`, the `pcrec_sb_text` field escape in `src/core/sb.c`), so joining the two dumps on them is safe | yes |
| `order` | a positive integer, 1-based, dense per row (N `definitions` entries use 1..N) | yes |
| `predicate` | the option-scope TAG's own name, never hand-authored prose: `DEF_ALWAYS`, `DEF_MULTILINE`, `DEF_NOCAP`, `DEF_UCP_D`, `DEF_UCP_S`, `DEF_UCP_W`, `DEF_UCP_P`, `DEF_UCP_T`, `DEF_ENCODING_UTF8`, and the two reserved tags `DEF_NEWLINE_CONV` and `DEF_LIB_NAME_BOUND` that have no producer yet — the closed enum `DefTag` in `src/core/internal.h` | yes, closed |
| `definition` | by entry kind. `DEFK_STR`: the core-syntax text (itself a valid probe pattern). `DEFK_TEXTFN` and `DEFK_BUILDER`: a human-readable TEMPLATE (`\cX = byte (X uppercased, then xor 0x40)`, `X<quant>+ ≡ (?>X<quant>)`), never spliced and never a live evaluation. `DEFK_SET`: the set's core-syntax spelling under `utf8`, with a `[fold-inert]` suffix where the set is fold-inert. `DEF_IDENTITY`: the row's own `syntax`, restated. `DEFK_ROW`: `= ` plus the target row's `syntax`, a REFERENCE to another row, never that row's resolved text printed twice. An entry keyed by an OPERAND rather than by an option-scope tag (the POSIX class family) is rendered `[[:<operand>:]] ≡ <definition>`, because the row's own `syntax` is one fixed example | free text, except that `DEF_IDENTITY` echoes `syntax` and `DEFK_ROW` echoes `= ` and the target |
| `applies` | `active` (the entry substitutes a different construct, a `DEFK_ROW` chain included) \| `identity` (restates the row's own primitive form) | yes, closed; read from the entry's `DefKind`, never inferred from absence |

1. <a id="s9-p2"></a>[9¶2] Identity is an explicit `DEF_IDENTITY` entry, never the absence of one. Two rows use it: `^`'s non-multiline entry (its primitive form, `A_BOL`, is core: `\A`'s alias) and the plain capturing group's non-`(?n)` entry (an ordinary `A_CAP`). `$`'s non-multiline entry is deliberately not identity: `A_EOL` is not core under full reduction (it aliases `\Z`, which reduces to `(?=\n?\z)`), so the entry is a `DEFK_ROW` chaining to `\Z`'s own row, which carries the substitution exactly once. `pcrec_def_resolve` (`src/parse/definitions.c`) walks through a `DEFK_ROW` entry, depth-bounded against a mis-edited cycle, so a caller never sees one.
2. <a id="s9-p3"></a>[9¶3] The `bare` kind (`RK_BARE`) has four `--list-syntax` rows, of which `^`, `$` and the plain capturing group `(...)` have definitions (`${name}` has none). It is a no-doorway kind like `quant-suffix` (§2): the dumps and `pcrec_def_resolve` reach its rows by iterating `pcrec_registry()`, never by a parse-time dispatch, so the base tier pays no lookup. `^`'s `DEF_MULTILINE` entry is `\A|(?<=\n)(?!\z)`; `$`'s is `(?=\n)|\z`; the capturing group's `DEF_NOCAP` entry is the `(?n)` builder, `(?n)(X) ≡ (?:X)`.
3. <a id="s9-p4"></a>[9¶4] A construct with two spellings shares one row. `\x{…}` and bare `\xHH` are one construct: the `\x` row's `DEFK_TEXTFN` template names both (`\xHH or \x{HHHH} = byte HH..HHHH (hex)`) and its textfn (`pcrec_def_text_hex`) is the one decode site for both. A construct that is LEXICAL — `\Q…\E`, `(?#…)`, which the lexer strips before any construct is recognised — has no definition and no row in this table.
4. <a id="s9-p5"></a>[9¶5] `--list-definitions` shares its source with the resolver it describes: `kind`, `selector`, `syntax`, `predicate` and `definition` are read off the same `RegRow.definitions` arrays `pcrec_def_resolve` walks at option-resolution time. It therefore proves what the table THINKS its definitions are; it is not evidence that a definition string parses to core-only vocabulary or matches what the construct it stands for matches. The structural side is `tests/registry/definitions_check.c`: every `DEFK_STR`/POSIX definition parses under `--features all`, every builder's and `DEFK_TEXTFN`'s output passes `pcrec_ast_all_core` (an exhaustive `AKind` switch), and every non-NULL `definitions` list ends in a `DEF_ALWAYS` entry, so `pcrec_def_resolve`'s fall-through is an `assert`, never a silent NULL. `tests/registry/run_definitions_tests.sh` adds that the tag evaluator `pcrec_def_tag_applies` has exactly one call site in `src/`, so `predicate`'s values cannot be second-guessed by a hidden second evaluator.
5. <a id="s9-p6"></a>[9¶6] The semantic side is `tests/registry/run_definitions_oracle.sh`, the option-matrix self-oracle: per row, over the option matrix, through the real tag evaluator, the table's resolved definition agrees with the row's own shipped construct, and that construct agrees with libpcre2. It skips loudly without libpcre2.
6. <a id="s9-p7"></a>[9¶7] `--list-definitions` takes `--flavour` exactly as `--list-syntax` does (`cli.md` §2): it walks the same `RegRow`s, filtered identically, so an unfiltered dump would print a definition for a construct `--list-syntax --flavour=X` says does not exist. It takes no pattern and no `-o`; it is a syntax query (`cli.md` §1).

<a id="s10"></a>
## 10. Where every table surface is documented

| # | surface | documented |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--list-syntax` | §2 |
| 2 | `--list-verbs` | §4 |
| 3 | `--list-families` | §5 |
| 4 | `--list-axes` | §6 |
| 5 | `--list-definitions` | §9 |
| 6 | `--list-limits` | `docs/spec/limits.md` §3 and `cli.md` §2 |
| 7 | `--list-schema` | `docs/spec/rxt_format.md`, "The schema and its surface", and `cli.md` §2 |

<a id="s10-p1"></a>[10¶1] The first five describe pcrec's own construct and axis registries, this document's subject. `--list-schema` describes the `.rxt` file format, whose contract lives with the format; a column table here would be a second home for it. The remaining table surfaces — `--list-source`, `--emit-ir`, `--emit-facts`, `--list-analyses`, `--list-analysis` — are listed with their producer shapes in `table_contract.md` §1.
